pike.text: I've secured the scene, {sir}. Nobody in or out. Except you. And the coroner. And Mr. Hale, who popped in for his reading glasses.
So, secured in the sense that a sieve is.

choice.text: What do you make of it, Pike?

pike_marla.text: Marla Quint. Eleven years on the show. She's in the control room, behind the glass. She rang it in at ten past three. You can talk to her on the intercom.
She hasn't cried. The book says that's suspicious.
The book has never worked nights.

pike_gordon.text: Gordon Hale, station manager. Over by the door; you'll need to turn round. He came across from Rudy's bar when he saw our cars.
He's asked twice when he can have his booth back.
Grief takes people differently. Some of them go straight to real estate.

pike_nudge.text: {sir}. Mr. Hale's started to sweat. The book says that's significant.
For once, Pike, the book and I agree. Come and find me when it's time to name someone. Or I'll find you.

accuse_gordon.text: I don't think the DA accepts faces.
You have nothing that contradicts Gordon Hale yet. Show him evidence first.

gordon_solid.text: Mr. Hale. You went home at eleven, you say.
Your car didn't. It was in the lot at four minutes past one.
And you were in this booth after 12:40, with a red pen and an opinion.
You spent the rest of the night at Rudy's, making sure a whole bar listened to a tape you'd started yourself.
And you threaded it like a man who signs the cheques for the people who thread it.
He was walking out on Friday. Thirty-one years I've kept this station breathing.
And tonight you kept him talking for seventy minutes after he'd stopped. Say what you like, Mr. Hale. That's management.
Gordon Hale, you have the right to remain silent.

do: remember You closed the Calloway case with evidence that will stand up.
gordon_solid.text: At this station, that's a change of format.

gordon_thin.text: Mr. Hale, I'm arresting you for the murder of Desmond Calloway.
On what? One loose thread and a feeling? My lawyer has eaten breakfast on more than that.
{sir}, are we sure we've got enough?

choice.text: We've got the right man. The rest is paperwork.

do: remember You arrested Gordon Hale before the case against him was finished.
gordon_thin_go.text: Gordon Hale, you have the right to remain silent. Which the book says you should strongly consider.

accuse_marla.text: Ms. Quint. It's your tape and your key. Your handwriting stops at 1:04, and somebody Dez called 'the Boss' walks in at 1:26.
He called me that because I told him when to stop talking. It's the only promotion I ever got.
Eleven years, Detective. Do you honestly think I'd thread it wrong?

marla_wrong.text: Marla Quint, you have the right to remain silent.
I've had eleven years of practice.

do: remember You charged Marla Quint with a murder she didn't commit.
marla_wrong.text: Tragic. Truly. Pike, was it? When can I have my booth back?

marla.text: You hold down the talkback button. The woman behind the glass takes her time looking up.
Keep the button held, Detective, or I only get half of every sentence. Story of my life.

marla_hub.if: marla_admitted and marla_trust >= 1 and not clue.gordon_car

choice.text: Who has keys to the tape cabinet?

marla_night.text: You know it now. I walked out at 1:04. I came back at three to apologise to him, God help me.
I was at the board all night. Dez did the show. At ten past three I looked up and he wasn't moving.
I thought he'd passed out. It wouldn't have been the first time. It wouldn't have been the fortieth.

marla_dez.text: He could make a stranger feel like the only other person awake in the city. He did it four hours a night. Then he went home and didn't return a single call.
He was wonderful to everyone he'd never met.

marla_tape.text: I cut it two years ago. Seventy minutes of his best calls, trimmed so nobody mentions a date. For the nights he couldn't stand up.
I've used it six times. The ratings were fine. Nobody ever told him.
Not me. I wasn't here to play it. And I'd have threaded it properly. I can load that deck in the dark. I have.
You were at the board all night and didn't notice the show had turned into a recording?

marla_keys.text: Two keys. Mine and Gordon's. He's never used his. He once asked me which end of a cassette was the front.

marla_shrug.text: I don't know what you want me to say about that, Detective. I produce. I don't interpret.

marla_boss.text: 'The Boss.' That was me, on air. A running bit. He'd say, 'The Boss says wrap it up,' and I'd play a whip crack.
Off air he only ever called one person boss, and he didn't mean it kindly.

marla_caught.text: We've done this one, Detective. I left. I'm not proud of it.
Your call sheet stops at 1:04. At 1:26, line three got through to Dez without anyone screening it. You weren't at the board, Ms. Quint.

choice.text: Eleven years of live radio, and now you go quiet?

marla_caught.text: At one o'clock, during the news, he told me he was leaving. Coastal Radio. Syndication. I asked where I fitted in. He said, 'Marla, they have producers there.'
So I logged Walter and his ex-wife's boat, put the pencil down, and walked out. Eleven years, and the only time I've ever left a live show.
I sat in my car by the river and listened to him carry on perfectly well without me.
No. I recognised the Owl's sister's wedding. I thought, the old bastard's found my tape. I was nearly flattered.
I lied because walking off a live board is the one thing you don't do. Isn't that stupid? He's dead, and I was worried about my reference.

marla_letter.text: I've seen it, Detective. Once was plenty.
'A chair that reclines.' That's what he put. Eleven years and he's leaving for furniture.
Does he say anything about the show? About... any of us?

choice.text: He mentions you. Says you were the best part of it. (Lie)
He doesn't mention you. I'm sorry.

do: remember You told Marla Quint that Dez's letter praised her. It doesn't mention her.
marla_lie.text: Thank you. For telling me that.

marla_truth.text: No. Well. He'd have had to stop talking about himself for a whole line.
Thank you for not dressing it up. People do, around here. It's a hazard of the trade.

marla_car.text: One more thing, since you've been decent with me. When I walked out at 1:04, Gordon's car was in the lot. The green one, in the space with his name on it.
He'll have told you he goes home at eleven. He does, usually. His car didn't.

gordon.text: Detective. Gordon Hale, I manage the station. Terrible thing. Terrible. Do you have any idea how long the booth will be... unavailable?

choice.text: Did you know Dez was leaving?
What happens to the station now?

gordon_night.text: Left here at eleven, same as always. I don't stay for the show. I've heard it.
Went home, couldn't settle, walked over to Rudy's about half past one. Stayed until the sirens.
We had the show on. The whole bar heard Dez take that Owl woman's call at a quarter past two. I said, 'That's my boy.' Ask anyone.

gordon_leaving.text: Leaving? Dez? That's news to me. Well. That's tragic twice over.
(He counted. People in shock don't usually count.)

gordon_station.text: We'll manage. There's insurance on him. Standard, for talent. A key-man policy. I'd forgotten all about it until tonight.

gordon_shrug.text: I'm sure that's very interesting to somebody.

gordon_iris.text: The Owl? She'd say anything to get on the air. That's the business model.
(Her word won't move him. I need what it adds up to.)

gordon_tape.text: Never seen it before. Tapes are Marla's department.
(Not enough on its own. I should work out what that tape means first.)

gordon_chair.text: Marla walked off a live show? Well, there you are. I'd look at her, if I were you. Which I'm glad I'm not.

gordon_alibi.text: The tape runs seventy minutes and it ran out at 2:40. It was started at half past one. What the whole bar heard at a quarter past two was a recording.
Your alibi, Mr. Hale, is that a tape recorder was working.
Then that's Marla's doing. It's her tape. Ask her.

gordon_letter.text: You went home at eleven. He typed this at 12:40. And this is your pen.
...I came back for my reading glasses. He handed me that. I wrote something sharp on it and I left. He was alive and pleased with himself, same as ever.
Those would be the reading glasses Officer Pike let you collect from a crime scene an hour ago.

gordon_amateur.text: Yes, yes. The threading. You said.
Whoever loaded that tape had a key to the cabinet and had never threaded the deck in their life. Marla Quint has done it every night for eleven years.
They do. They skip the tension arm, for one.

gordon_car.text: I've told you about the car.
Your car was in the lot at 1:04.
I walk home sometimes. For my heart.
And then back to Rudy's, past your own car. For your heart.
